name: RGB-D Plenoxel Mapping
text:
# RGB-D Plenoxel Mapping

Also called: RGB-D Plenoxel

## Overview
A dense mapping algorithm that extends the [Plenoxel](#8054-plenoxel.md) model to incorporate depth data from an RGB-D sensor, removing geometric ambiguities in gradient-less regions [S1]. Unlike [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) which suffers from geometric ambiguity in outward-facing scenes, this method uses depth sensors to ensure accurate geometry [S1].

## How it works
**Inputs and Outputs:**
*   **Inputs:** RGB images and corresponding depth maps from an RGB-D sensor; initial voxel grid parameters (opacity $\sigma$ and spherical harmonic coefficients).
*   **Outputs:** Optimized voxel grid parameters representing the scene geometry and appearance.

**Data Structures:**
The method builds upon the Plenoxel representation, which uses a voxel grid to store opacity ($\sigma$) and spherical harmonic (SH) coefficients for radiance [S1]. The specific bit-packing or layout of the voxel grid is not detailed in the sources, relying on the standard Plenoxel implementation [S1].

**Steps:**
1.  **Derive Analytical Derivatives:** Derive the analytical derivative equations for mapping in a voxel-based radiance field based on RGB-D data [S1]. This involves calculating gradients with respect to the voxel parameters using both RGB [color loss](#9563-photometric-loss-rawnerf-variant.md) and depth consistency loss.
2.  **[CUDA](#3671-dual-contouring-2d-cuda.md) Implementation:** Implement the mapping optimization in CUDA to leverage the inherent speed of the Plenoxel model, which is more than two magnitudes faster than the [original NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) algorithm [S1].
3.  **Optimization:** Perform gradient-based optimization to minimize the difference between rendered RGB/depth and observed RGB-D data [S1].

**Formulas:**
The sources state that analytical derivative equations are derived for mapping and tracking but do not provide the explicit mathematical formulas [S1].

**Parameters:**
Typical values for learning rates or optimization steps are not given in the sources [S1].

**Edge Cases and Pitfalls:**
Standard NeRF implementations fail in scenes with sparse gradient coverage or outward-facing scenes, leading to invalid view synthesis outside the training pose distribution [S1]. The RGB-D Plenoxel method specifically addresses this by using depth data to resolve ambiguities in these gradient-less regions [S1].

## Subtopics

### Volumetric Dense Image-to-Model Tracking
A pose optimization algorithm that tracks camera motion by aligning the camera image to the volumetric dense map using [radiance field rendering equations](#8682-volume-rendering-integral.md) [S1]. Unlike sparse tracking which uses a subset of points, dense tracking uses all image and model information for smoother and more accurate trajectories [S1]. It derives analytical derivative equations for tracking in a voxel-based radiance field based on RGB-D data and implements the tracking optimization in CUDA [S1].

## Operating characteristics
The method leverages the inherent speed of the Plenoxel model, which is more than two magnitudes faster than the original NeRF algorithm [S1]. This efficiency enables a very fast mapping algorithm and a real-time, highly accurate tracking algorithm [S1]. The sources do not provide specific memory complexity or measured performance metrics beyond the relative speed comparison [S1].

## Background
The method is based on the Plenoxel algorithm, an analytical [radiance field representation](#11368-scene-representation-and-architecture.md) that uses a voxel grid instead of a neural network [S1]. It was introduced to make radiance field models more applicable for practical tasks like robotics and XR, where standard NeRF struggles with geometric ambiguity [S1]. The work was presented in 2024 [S1].
